patch.value: Design committed repository links local layers and typed obliteration

Add native repository composition and lifecycle operations: committed links pin authorized repository and revision identities, local layers overlay an instance without changing commits, and authorized obliteration produces a typed payload state distinct from garbage collection, missing data or corruption.

Committed links are reproducible and retain the linked repository authorization boundary; Local layers never alter commit identity and are visibly excluded from ordinary status; Obliteration is authorized audited and scoped by stable file identity; Checkout and verify distinguish obliterated content from missing and corrupt objects

value.text: Audit 2026-09-13: EXISTS — committed repository links are implemented as sparse linked instances (engine/instances.ts: instance link, shared object store, sparse views; test/instances.test.ts: 'a linked instance materializes its view, shares objects and keeps private state', 'concurrent instances share objects but never overwrite each other's state'). REMAINS — local layers that overlay an instance without changing commit identity are not implemented (grep for local-layer/overlay returns no matches). Typed obliteration is not implemented (grep for obliterate/Obliteration in engine/ returns no matches). Checkout and verify distinguishing obliterated content from missing and corrupt objects is not implemented. Two of four acceptance criteria are not met.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Baseline against the built package and a real disposable SDK tracker: a synthetic binary was staged and committed successfully; vcs link, vcs layer and vcs obliterate are absent, and the repository exposes no layer or obliteration API. Acceptance will pin a typed external repository revision and subset across a clone without transferring its payload or credentials; overlay tracked and new paths while preserving commit identity and excluding layers visibly from status and add; authorize FileId-scoped erasure across moves and revisions, byte-scan stored and decoded representations, distinguish obliterated/missing/corrupt state, and reject resurrection through stale fetch/import. The previous audit conflated local shared instances with committed external links. Full item, parent, linked research record and LORE.md were read; the removed historical research-doc link is superseded by LORE.md.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Design recorded first in docs/links-layers-obliteration.md: canonical typed committed links with explicit target authorization; private layer snapshots masked from staging/status and preserved across materialization; authorized FileId erasure with durable typed denial, full-store historical inventory, deduplication refusal, byte removal and non-resurrection at every object arrival boundary. Remote tombstones cannot silently authorize deletion of locally held content. Verification and checkout preserve the distinction between intentional erasure, missing data and corruption.

value.author: codex-sol-implementation
value.text: Implementation decision: typed link leaf objects carry only repository identity, exact commit ID and explicit file mappings. Resolution requires a separately authorized local target binding and creates a private layer. Layers preserve edited disk bytes across materialization and refuse removal without explicit edit discard. Erasure inventories all loose objects, indexes and registered instances under one store writer lock; unknown pack/cache artefacts and deduplication conflicts refuse before denial. Durable pending denial blocks all writes until authorized cleanup completes. After erasure, resumable payload-only batches refuse because they carry no FileId provenance; complete bundles preflight every tree and payload before publication.
